hypotheses.claim: The shadow-check in Attribute.js (`local_binding.node !== binding.node`) bails out even when the shadowing binding is declared entirely inside the handler function, so such handlers are not hoisted although they need no outer params.
evidence_refs: baseline compiled_client: button_1.__click inline arrow, button_2.__click = [on_click]
assertion ARE_EXPECTED_HOISTED_CALLBACK fails only for button_1 (shadowed local `index`)
hypotheses.prediction: Skipping the shadow bail when the resolved binding's declaration node lies within the target function's start/end range will hoist B's handler to a shared on_click while keeping A's (closes over each `index`) inline and C unchanged.
hypotheses.falsifier: If hoisting B yields a handler referencing the outer each `index` (wrong closure), or A/C hoisting changes, the positional check is wrong and another mechanism is needed.

hypotheses.claim: Alternative: bail based on scope depth — a binding declared inside the handler has binding.scope.function_depth greater than target_function.metadata.scope.function_depth, so it needs no hoisted param.
hypotheses.prediction: A function_depth-based skip also hoists B; identical result to the positional check unless metadata.scope is the enclosing scope rather than the function's own scope.
hypotheses.falsifier: If metadata.scope points at the enclosing scope (depths equal), the depth check never triggers and B stays inline.
